$comment: IPC bindings with no production caller. Each entry needs a REASON,
because an entry without one is indistinguishable from a defect
somebody recorded instead of fixing. Ratchet: may shrink, never grow.
GREW ONCE, from 7 to 18, and the reason is a widened SCOPE rather than
new dead code. myne-md/myne#609 scoped caller matching per binding tree:
callers are matched by name, and the flat caller list contained both `src`
and `mobile/src`, so a mobile binding was satisfied by a same-named desktop
caller. The twin modules are same-named by design, so the blind spot was as
wide as the twin set. Measured by flattening the roster back and reading
what the guard then says: TWELVE of the entries below go stale, which is
twelve bindings it would have called live. Two of those are not cosmetic
(`vault-unlock.ts:reportUserActivity` and `:isVaultUnlocked`).
The first version of this note claimed the measurement was the three prefs
setters #609 added. That was wrong, and it is left recorded rather than
quietly swapped, because it is the same class of error this guard exists to
catch: `bindingsInSource` requires a literal `invoke("plugin:x|y")` in the
function body, and every prefs setter goes through `writePref`, so the
guard never saw those three at all.
Seven older entries carried the literal `--record` placeholder as their
reason. It is 15 characters, so it passed the length check the ratchet uses,
which means the record could claim a reason nobody had written. The ratchet
now rejects that exact string, and all eighteen entries below were then
investigated one at a time and say what was actually found.
One entry LEFT this list in the same change and was not dead at all:
`clipboardTransport.ts:writeText` is imported as `writeText as
clipboardWriteText`, and the guard stripped the one line connecting the two
names before probing for the call. `importAliases` now resolves that, so
the record no longer carries a false statement about a live binding.

exempt.mobile/src/lib/attachments.ts:attachment: Mobile never maintains the RAM attachment-reference graph incrementally: the three reconcile bindings mirror the Rust commands, and the desktop's callers live in `src/notes/attachmentRefs.ts`, which mobile has no counterpart of. The cold case is covered, because `hydrate_attachment_refs_core` rebuilds the graph from the notes at unlock; what is missing is the within-session update, so on mobile an attachment's "used in N notes" count is as of the last unlock. Wiring it means a mobile note-save path calling this, which is a mobile attachments task and not a line of glue.

The query half of the same trio. It has no caller because mobile shows no "used in N notes" surface at all; the desktop's is `src/notes/attachmentRefs.ts`. Kept rather than deleted because the other two are kept: deleting one third of a trio would leave the next author reading a partial mirror of the Rust command set.

Same gap as `attachmentRefsApply` one entry up, on the delete side: nothing on mobile drops a hard-deleted note from the RAM ref graph, so within a session the graph over-reports until the next unlock rebuild. Over-reporting is the safe direction (the unused-attachment list stays fail-closed), which is why this is stale-count debt rather than a data-loss risk.
exempt.mobile/src/lib/export.ts:vaultExportCanc: Mobile's export flow offers no cancel. The desktop's `VaultExportModal.tsx` does, and calls its own `src/notes/vaultExport.ts` binding. So this is a mobile UI gap: the command and its ACL row are in place and the button is not.
exempt.mobile/src/lib/graph-layout-persist.ts:g: Called, but only from inside its own module (`hydrateGraphLayout(await graphLayoutRead())` at line 57), and a module cannot call itself into liveness by this guard's identity rule. So the binding is live and the EXPORT is what is dead. Left exported rather than made module-private because its desktop twin exports the same name, and the twin-drift guard reads the pair.

Same shape as `graphLayoutRead` one entry up: two same-module call sites (the debounced flush and `flushGraphLayoutNow`), no cross-module caller. Live binding, unnecessary export, kept for twin parity.
exempt.mobile/src/lib/reminders.ts:createRawRem: The UNWRAPPED notifier, exported for tests that need to see the bytes handed to the plugin; production goes through `createReminderNotifier`, which wraps it at the factory so an opaque identifier cannot be got wrong at a call site (`threat-model.md` section 7). A test-only export is exactly what this guard does not count as a caller, and here that is the intended shape rather than debt.
exempt.mobile/src/lib/reminders.ts:createRemind: Nothing on mobile asks for notification permission yet, because the whole reminders pass is unwired: `mobile/src/lib/reminderPass.ts` has zero production callers and is a recorded `check-unwired.mjs` violation. This binding is one leaf of that, and wiring it in isolation would produce a permission prompt for a feature that never runs.
exempt.mobile/src/lib/snapshots.ts:snapshotPrun: Mobile captures snapshots (the two `MobileHooks` snapshot hooks are live) and offers no prune control. The desktop's caller is in `src/notes/snapshots.ts`. Debt with a size consequence rather than a correctness one: the per-note snapshot set on a phone is only bounded by whatever the backend retention does.
exempt.mobile/src/lib/transcribe.ts:readTranscr: Reads an already-cached transcript without re-running the engine. Mobile's voice flow always runs the engine and consumes the result from that run, so nothing asks for the cache. There is no desktop counterpart by this name, so the entry is not a twin gap; it is an accessor written ahead of a surface that would use it.
exempt.mobile/src/lib/vault-indices.ts:vaultInd: Mobile shows no unlinked-mention surface, which is what this query feeds. No desktop binding of this name exists either, so nothing here is a twin gap: the command is registered and the surface that would ask it has not been built on either client.

Feeds the "isolated notes" filter of the graph view. Desktop calls it from `src/notes/components/GraphView.tsx`; mobile's graph landed with the layout and culling work (MYND-530) and without that filter, so the binding is the mobile graph's missing option rather than dead code.
exempt.mobile/src/lib/vault-status.ts:probeVaul: A diagnostic probe with a usage example in its own doc comment and no caller on EITHER client, which is why its desktop twin is the next entry. Neither client has a surface that reports vault status, so this is a helper written ahead of one.
exempt.mobile/src/lib/vault-unlock.ts:isVaultUn: The slot probe. Mobile's stage machine (`src/lib/stage.ts`) carries the unlocked state in React and transitions on the unlock command's own result, so nothing re-asks the backend. Not the same class as `reportUserActivity` below: a probe nobody calls costs nothing, because the authority is the backend slot either way.
exempt.mobile/src/lib/vault-unlock.ts:reportUse: The window-level heartbeat for the BACKEND idle timer, and it has no caller because mobile spawns no backend idle timer: `auto_lock::spawn_idle_lock_timer` is called from `src-tauri/src/lib.rs` and has no counterpart in `mobile/src-tauri/src/lib.rs`. Be precise about what that does and does not mean, because the first version of this entry said auto-lock on idle 'does not exist' on mobile and a reviewer refuted it: mobile DOES lock on idle, in the WebView (`mobile/src/app/flows/EditorFlow.tsx`, clamped by `effectiveMobileAutoLockSecs` with no disable path, and its own comment names the A6 envelope it implements). That timer is JS-local, so it needs no heartbeat. What is absent is the backend clock, not the control, and `threat-model.md` A6 is unaffected. Writing the stronger claim into a checked-in record was the more expensive mistake of the two, because the next reader would have re-implemented a control that is already there.
exempt.mobile/src/lib/workspace-persist.ts:work: Same shape as the graph-layout pair: called from inside its own module (line 132, the read-modify-write that splices mobile's folder-expand set into a descriptor a desktop pane tree may share), never across a module boundary. Live binding, unnecessary export, kept for twin parity.
The write half of the same read-modify-write, called at line 150 in its own module. Live binding, unnecessary export, kept for twin parity.
exempt.src/lib/vault-status.ts:probeVaultStatus: The desktop twin of the mobile entry above, dead for the same reason and on the same evidence: no client has a vault-status surface. It is the only entry in this record that is not mobile, and it was invisible while caller matching was flat, because the two same-named bindings answered for each other.
